answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce token deposit before its identity earns voting or payment rights, then slash that deposit when a ledger-proven fraud claim succeeds. Creating a thousand aliases no longer creates influence for free: every identity needs capital, and each can lose it. The ledge is the cost of entry, not a magic shield—an attacker with enough funds can still buy many identities. Ferrous discipline in enforcement and a prism of independent evidence help distinguish fraud from honest error.
